results.question: Explain SGPA calculation and how a repeated course affects CGPA.
results.expected_answer: Credit-weighted grade points over attempted credits; CGPA uses most recent grade even if lower, not highest.
results.answer:
The Semester Grade Point Average (SGPA) is calculated using the formula: SGPA = (P1*C1 + P2*C2 + P3*C3 + P4*C4)/C, where P1, P2, P3, and P4 are the grade points earned in courses, C1, C2, C3, and C4 are the credit hours of the respective courses studied in the semester, and C is the total number of credits attempted in the semester (C = C1+C2+C3+C4) [S1] [S5]. 

When calculating the Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) for repeated courses, only the most recent grade points are used, even if they are less than the earlier attempts [S3].

5. Academic Assessment 
5.1 The performance of students is assessed during the semester 
through midterm exams, assignments, quizzes, case studies or 
any other method conside red appropriate by the course 
instructor and the  University and communicated to the  
students at the start of a course. 
5.2 The semester work will normally contribute 50% towards the 
final gr ade, while the fin al e xamination will contribute the 
remaining 50% of the  total marks. A  letter grade will be 
awarded to each student based on his/her overall academic 
performance in a course. 
5.3 Any deviation f rom Rule 5.2 above if n ecessitated by the 
nature of course will be made with the approval of Dean of the 
Faculty. 
Academic Warning/Probation 
5.4 Minimum CGPA required to avoid aca demic warning is 2. 00 
for all undergraduate programs. 
5.5 If at the end of a semester (including summer semester) CGPA 
drops b elow 2.00, w arning is issued, and warning count is 
incremented by one. 
5.6 If CGPA remains b elow 2.00 for 3 c onsecutive semesters, 
warning count becomes three and the admission of student at 
the University is automatically closed.

results.question: For FYP-I, what are the normal requirements and who can allow a deficiency of one or two courses?
results.expected_answer: Normal all study-plan courses and warning count0; second-last semester/ability graduate following; HoD can allow1deficiency Director2; FYP-II after successfulFYP-I.
results.answer:
The retrieved rules require a zero warning count for FYP-I. The course-deficiency permissions do not establish permission to waive that condition. They are discretionary, not automatic:

> warning count must be zero to register for FYP- I. [S1]

> The Head of department can allow registration in FYP-I where there is a deficiency of one course. [S1]

> The Director of the campus can allow registration in F YP-I where there is deficiency of two courses. [S1]
